title: String tasks
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Programming 2: data structures, files and subprograms
source: Seeded from computing/y10 lesson 29 (Pupil PDF worksheet: string tasks)
intro: Lesson 29: Manipulating strings: length, position, slices and case. To understand how to manipulate strings using length, indexing, slicing, concatenation and case conversion

questions.q: For s = 'Al-Kahf', write expressions for: its length, its last character, 'Kahf', and it in capitals.
questions.model: I do: len(s): A, l, -, K, a, h, f = 7. s[-1] = 'f'. 'Kahf' starts at index 3 and ends at 6, so s[3:7]. s.upper() = 'AL-KAHF'.

questions.q: Pupil PDF: write a program that inputs a sentence and outputs its length, the number of vowels and the sentence with the first letter capitalised.
questions.a: len(s); loop counting characters in 'aeiouAEIOU'; s[0].upper() + s[1:].
questions.model: The teacher writes the vowel loop: count = 0; for ch in s: if ch in 'aeiouAEIOU': count = count + 1

questions.a: s[::-1] or a loop from the end.

questions.q: Stretch: check whether a word is a palindrome.
Back to our ponder: A school email is made from a pupil's name, like 'yahmed24'. How could a program build it automatically?
questions.a: Take the first letter of the first name, the surname, a number, then make it lower case: string manipulation.
